items.title: Eddie Locke interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, NY, January 13, 2001
items.q: One of those chordal, Chopin things, it’s all chords you know?

ctx.x: I guess he liked to have a normal—

It was a normal, buddy thing. And a little father, you know he was like, he always was encouraging me. I learned how to write music — because I’d never studied music you know — but I learned all the chords and all that stuff you know. And that’s another thing © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -16-

about those guys. He’d be back in the kitchen in his apartment and I might just play a triad, like a C, and he’d say “yeah, Locke, that’s good.” You know what I mean? But he wouldn’t be trying to B.S. me. And I got a book called, you know like those little — how they take classical pieces and shorten them and put them in these books? And he had one of them. And he said “you get one of these books.” One of those chordal, Chopin things, it’s all chords you know? And he said “now you’re going to learn how to play…
